# Company 065 — Autonomous QA-as-a-Service

**Company ID:** `company:future:065`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:065`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-065-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no production test execution against customer systems without explicit authorization and environment safeguards.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide continuous, evidence-backed quality assurance across web, mobile, desktop, API and workflow surfaces using synthetic users, deterministic assertions, visual checks, accessibility, compatibility, performance and controlled security testing.

Problem: product teams miss regressions because test coverage is fragmented, manual QA is slow, test data is brittle and release gates often verify only happy paths.

Value: broader automated coverage, faster bug reproduction, stable release evidence, reusable test packs and independent verification separated from the builder/executor.

## Complete product tree

Web QA; Mobile QA; API QA; Desktop QA; Workflow/E2E QA; Functional Tests; Visual Regression; Accessibility QA; Browser/Device Compatibility; Localization QA; Performance/Load; Resilience/Chaos Test Planning; Security Regression Checks; Synthetic User Journeys; Test Generation; Test Data/Synthetic Fixture Builder; Bug Reproduction; Evidence/Replay; Release Gate; Regression Pack Marketplace; API/SDK/CLI; CI/CD Integration; Managed QA; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical QA Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: requirements/spec links, test cases, fixtures, environments, browsers/devices, selectors/contracts, expected results, screenshots, traces/logs, accessibility rules, performance thresholds, retries, flake classification, deterministic replay, risk severity, bug evidence, test ownership/version, release candidate identity and independent verifier status.

Customers: startups, SaaS, agencies, enterprises, mobile/web teams, API providers, ecommerce, regulated software, QA consultancies, platform vendors and internal engineering groups.

Verticals: ecommerce checkout, finance-adjacent software, health administrative systems, accessibility-sensitive public services, B2B SaaS, mobile apps, marketplaces, developer platforms and legacy software. Domain packs encode workflows without weakening independent QA.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may infer test cases from specs/diffs, prioritize risk, interpret failures and propose reproduction steps. Deterministic test runners/assertions own pass/fail whenever possible. Visual/model judgments require confidence/evidence and should not replace explicit requirements.

Architecture: requirement/test registry, environment/device matrix, isolated runners, browser/mobile/API adapters, visual diff, accessibility engines, performance/load tools, fixture/synthetic data service, trace/artifact store, flake classifier, replay harness, release-gate policy and independent QA identity.

## Agent tree

Test Planner; Functional QA Agent; API QA Agent; Visual QA Agent; Accessibility Agent; Compatibility Agent; Performance Agent; Security Regression Agent; Localization QA Agent; Synthetic User Agent; Bug Reproducer; Flake Investigator; Evidence Agent; Independent Release Verifier.

## Deterministic services

Test runner orchestration; environment isolation; selector/contract validation; screenshot hashing/diff; accessibility rule engines; API schema assertions; load scheduling; retry/flake policy; artifact capture; test versioning; deterministic replay; release gate and pass/fail evidence.

## Workflow tree

Ingest requirements/diff/release candidate → build/update risk-based test plan → prepare isolated environment/fixtures → run deterministic suites in parallel → collect artifacts/traces → classify failures vs flakes → reproduce/minimize bug → route unresolved model-based judgments to review → rerun fixes → independent verifier confirms acceptance → issue release-gate evidence, never deployment authority.

## Integrations / API / data

Git/source control, CI/CD, issue trackers, design/screenshot references, browser/device farms, app builds, API schemas, observability, accessibility tools, test-management systems and release platforms. APIs for plans, tests, runs, artifacts, failures, reproductions and gate evidence.

Data: requirements, tests, fixtures, runs, environments, artifacts, screenshots, logs, failures, classifications, bugs, acceptance evidence and trend metrics. Customer test data stays isolated and secrets are reference-only.

## Monetization / distribution

Test runs/minutes, devices/browsers, suites, repositories/apps, concurrent runners, seats, load volume, enterprise/private, API/OEM, managed QA and premium vertical packs. Distribution via CI/devtool marketplaces, agencies and engineering consultancies.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Runners are sandboxed, credentials scoped to test environments, production testing disabled by default, no destructive chaos/security test without explicit authorization, data redaction, artifact retention policy and customer isolation. QA must remain independent from the implementation Agent for high-risk acceptance.

## Failure / edge cases

Flaky network/UI, nondeterministic animations, test pollution, shared-state races, captcha/2FA, third-party outage, browser version change, accessibility false positive, visual anti-aliasing drift, performance noisy neighbor, bad fixture, test passes wrong environment, synthetic user creates real side effect. Environment identity and cleanup are mandatory.

## Scale / overlap

Single repo regression suite → cross-platform QA service → autonomous quality-control infrastructure. Overlap #3 AI quality-control evaluates AI systems; #065 evaluates software/products broadly; #53 release autopilot consumes QA evidence; #56 synthetic data supplies fixtures.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** independent verifier identity, test/evidence/artifact contracts, environment isolation, replay, synthetic side-effect fencing, quality-gate interfaces.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already needs independent QA and evidence; reverse-map should formalize reusable Testing Factory seams.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** isolated runner registry, environment matrix, artifact store, replay and test orchestration.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer device/browser farms, connectors, vertical packs, billing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large distributed runner fleet and marketplace of evaluated test packs.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: web/mobile/API/desktop/workflow/functional/visual/accessibility/compat/localization/performance/security/synthetic/repro/release gate/API.
2. Feature Tree: requirements/tests/fixtures/env/devices/assertions/screenshots/traces/a11y/perf/retries/flakes/evidence/versioning.
3. Customer Tree: startup/SaaS/agency/enterprise/mobile/web/API/ecommerce/regulated/QA consultancy/platform vendor.
4. Vertical Tree: commerce/finance-adjacent/health admin/public services/B2B/mobile/marketplace/devplatform/legacy.
5. Brain Tree: test generation/prioritization/failure interpretation; deterministic assertions dominate pass/fail.
6. Agent Tree: planner/functional/API/visual/a11y/compat/perf/security/localization/synthetic/reproducer/flake/evidence/verifier.
7. Service Tree: runners/isolation/assertions/diff/a11y/schema/load/retry/artifacts/version/replay/gates.
8. Workflow Tree: ingest→plan→prepare→run→capture→classify/reproduce→rerun→independent verify→evidence.
9. Integration Tree: Git/CI/issues/design/device farms/builds/APIs/observability/a11y/test management/releases.
10. Data Tree: requirements/tests/fixtures/runs/env/artifacts/failures/bugs/evidence/trends.
11. API Tree: plans/tests/runs/artifacts/failures/reproduction/gates.
12. Monetization Tree: runs/minutes/devices/suites/apps/concurrency/seats/load/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: CI/devtool marketplaces/agencies/consultancies/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: planning/execution/reproduction/regression automated; ambiguous acceptance and destructive tests gated.
15. Moat Tree: test/repro corpus, vertical packs, runner reliability, cross-platform evidence.
16. Platform Tree: QA service→autonomous testing factory→software quality infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: false pass/flaky failure/production side effect/secret leak/wrong environment/biased visual judgment.
18. Scale Tree: repo→portfolio→distributed global test fleet.
19. Spinoff Tree: visual QA/accessibility/repro runner modules; AI evaluation remains separate Company 003.
20. Command Center Dependencies: Agency, independent verification, artifacts, environments, resource governor, security, release gates.
21. Design-Now Requirements: test/evidence identities, independent verifier separation and side-effect-safe fixtures.
22. Build-Now Requirements: formalize Testing/Evaluation Factory primitives reusable by Command Center and future companies.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer runner fleets/device farms/integrations/marketplace/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: tests are generated, run, reproduced and regression-maintained continuously; humans resolve ambiguous requirements and approve high-risk release exceptions.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into AI-specific evaluation, accessibility monitoring, release control or synthetic data products already represented.

# Company 066 — AI Runtime Security Gateway

**Company ID:** `company:future:066`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:066`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-066-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no external gateway deployment, customer traffic interception or production policy enforcement.

## Business identity
Purpose: sit between AI agents/models and tools/data/actions to enforce identity, permissions, risk, content security, policy, DLP and real-time allow/challenge/block decisions.

## Product tree
Agent Firewall; Model Firewall; Tool-Call Gateway; API Proxy; Data-Access Gateway; Browser/Code/Infra Action Gate; Financial/Communication Gate; Identity/Delegation Verifier; Prompt-Injection Defense; Malware/DLP Scanner; Behavioral Anomaly Engine; Policy/Risk Engine; Quarantine; Approval/Step-Up; Audit/Replay; Shadow/Simulation; Red-Team Harness; SDK/Sidecar/Proxy; Enterprise Appliance; Industry Policy Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: actor/model/tool/resource identity, request intent, input/output provenance, sensitivity, permissions, delegated scope, budget, action reversibility/blast radius, normal-behavior baseline, content threats, DLP classes, policy version, decision reason, approval state, execution receipt, replay and incident links.
Customers: agent platforms, enterprises, AI SaaS, developer platforms, regulated organizations, security teams, AI infrastructure vendors.
Verticals: finance-adjacent, healthcare admin, legal ops, enterprise IT, software engineering, ecommerce, support, procurement; each needs policy/data/action packs.

## Brain capability / architecture
AI may classify intent/threat/context and explain risk; deterministic deny-by-default policy owns enforcement. Architecture: identity/delegation service, policy engine, risk scorer, trusted/untrusted content segmentation, DLP/malware/injection scanners, tool schema registry, secure proxy, approval broker, behavior model, audit ledger, replay/simulation and kill switch.

## Agent tree
Policy Analyst; Runtime Monitor; Threat Classifier; Behavior Analyst; DLP Agent; Tool Schema Agent; Approval Coordinator; Incident Agent; Red-Team Agent; Audit/Forensics Agent; Policy QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
AuthN/AuthZ; scope subset checks; schema validation; rate/budget limits; action class/risk lookup; secret redaction; content quarantine; circuit breakers; one-time authorization consume; idempotency; signed receipts; policy versioning.

## Workflow
AI/tool request → authenticate actor/runtime → bind delegated authority → classify resource/action/content → scan threats/DLP/injection → evaluate policy/risk/budget → allow/challenge/block/quarantine → step-up if needed → execute only through scoped connector → verify receipt → update behavior/audit → incident/escalation if anomalous.

## Integrations / API / data
Agent frameworks, model gateways, MCP/A2A/custom tools, APIs, browsers, code runners, clouds, databases, file systems, communication/payment providers, SIEM/GRC. Data: identities, requests, policy versions, scans, decisions, receipts, incidents; never centralize raw secrets unnecessarily.

## Monetization / distribution
Per request/tool call/agent/protected app, seats, policy packs, enterprise/private appliance, SDK/API, managed security. Distribution through AI developer/security ecosystems, cloud marketplaces and enterprise security channels.

## Security/privacy/legal
This company is itself a security boundary: fail closed on unknown identity/policy, tamper-evident decisions, isolated tenants, no model-only enforcement, emergency global kill, policy rollback, privacy-preserving telemetry.

## Failure / edge cases
Prompt injection inside tool output, compromised trusted tool, confused deputy, replay, stale authorization, identity impersonation, model provider outage, scanner outage, policy conflict, oversized payload, encrypted/malformed content, time-of-check/time-of-use drift, partial action execution.

## Scale / overlap
Agent SDK → enterprise gateway → foundational agentic-security control plane. Overlap #4 governance, #5 audit trail, #67 injection firewall, #73 secrets, #91 agent identity. #066 owns real-time runtime enforcement.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** central action taxonomy, identity/delegation, deny-default policy, trusted/untrusted provenance, one-time authorization, audit, kill switch, policy versioning.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already requires most of these; reverse-map should treat its own protected-action boundary as the internal reference implementation.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** external tenant/gateway SDK, secure proxy, customer policy packs.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial gateway/SDK/appliance.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global low-latency enforcement fabric.

18. Scale Tree: app→enterprise→global fleet.

# Company 067 — Prompt-Injection Firewall API

**Company ID:** `company:future:067`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:067`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-067-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer traffic processing or production policy enforcement.

## Business identity
Purpose: detect, segment, score, sanitize or quarantine malicious instructions hidden inside content consumed by AI systems, while preserving useful data and instruction hierarchy.

## Product tree
Text Scan API; Email/Document/Webpage Scanner; PDF/OCR Scanner; Image-Text Scanner; Tool-Output Scanner; Search/RAG Gateway; Knowledge-Base Ingest Gate; Browser-Agent Shield; Email-Agent Shield; Sanitizer/Quarantine; Trusted-Untrusted Segmentation; Instruction-Hierarchy Analyzer; Encoding/Obfuscation Detector; Policy Packs; Threat Intel/Rules Feed; Developer SDK; Reverse Proxy/Sidecar; Enterprise Private Appliance; Red-Team Corpus; Evaluation Suite.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: source provenance, trusted/untrusted regions, direct/indirect injection, jailbreak patterns, hidden text/markup, encoded payloads, malicious links/attachments, instruction override attempts, tool-manipulation cues, suspicious data exfiltration requests, risk/confidence, sanitization diff, quarantine reason and model/tool context.
Customers: AI SaaS, RAG vendors, agent platforms, enterprises, browser/email agents, search/knowledge platforms, security vendors and developers.
Verticals: enterprise knowledge, support, finance-adjacent, healthcare admin, legal document systems, developer agents, ecommerce, research/search.

## Brain capability / architecture
Use layered deterministic parsing, heuristics/signatures, content provenance, structural analysis and specialized classifiers/models. Brain may classify ambiguous attacks but must never decide authority from the content itself. Architecture: source parser, trust-zone annotator, decoder/normalizer, threat rules, classifier ensemble, sanitizer, quarantine store, evaluation corpus, versioned policy and API gateway.

## Agent tree
Content Intake Agent; Normalization Agent; Injection Classifier; Obfuscation Agent; Trust-Segment Agent; RAG Guard Agent; Tool-Output Guard Agent; Sanitization Agent; Red-Team Agent; Threat-Rule Curator; QA/Evaluation Agent.

## Deterministic services
MIME/HTML/PDF parsing; encoding decode; Unicode normalization; hidden-content detection; trust labels; allow/deny patterns; schema-preserving sanitization; hash/version; rate limits; tenant isolation; signed scan receipt.

## Workflow
Content arrives → classify source/provenance → parse/decode/normalize → segment trusted system instructions from untrusted data → detect injection/obfuscation/tool-manipulation → score → allow with labels / sanitize / quarantine / block → return machine-readable receipt → downstream model/tool gateway must still enforce its own authorization → feedback/evaluation.

## Integrations / API / data
Email, browsers, web fetch/search, RAG pipelines, document ingestion, OCR, knowledge bases, agent frameworks, model gateways, security/SIEM. Data: scan metadata, hashes, findings, sanitized deltas, labels and feedback; minimize retention of customer raw content.

# Company 068 — AI Cost & Model Routing Optimizer

**Company ID:** `company:future:068`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:068`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-068-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no paid-model activation, provider purchase, quota change or customer routing.

## Business identity
Purpose: choose the most suitable AI model/provider/configuration for each task under explicit quality, privacy, latency, reliability and cost constraints.

## Product tree
Model Catalog; Benchmark Registry; Task Classifier; Complexity Estimator; Routing Policy Engine; Cost/Latency/Quality Optimizer; Privacy/Data-Residency Router; Local-vs-Hosted Selector; Fallback/Outage Router; Ensemble/Consensus Planner; Prompt/Context Compression; Semantic Cache; Response Cache; Batch/Scheduled Inference; Quota/Budget Manager; Provider Health; Model Retirement/Migration; ROI Dashboard; Routing Simulator; API Gateway/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical Evaluation Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: model/provider/version, modalities, context length, tool/function support, regions, privacy class, benchmark scores, task families, price units, latency distributions, success/verification rates, quota, availability, cached equivalence, fallback graph, quality floors, cost ceilings, SLA, evidence and route version.
Customers: AI SaaS, agent platforms, enterprises, developers, model gateways, data/AI teams and software vendors.
Verticals: coding, document extraction, customer support, research, analytics, vision, audio/voice, regulated private workloads and high-throughput automation.

## Brain capability / architecture
Routing should primarily be deterministic constrained optimization over measured data; ML may predict quality/latency/cost; LLMs may classify task semantics but must not control budgets without policy. Architecture: provider/model registry, benchmark/eval store, task ontology, policy constraints, optimization engine, health/quota telemetry, cache, fallback DAG, privacy router, experiment service and cost ledger.

## Agent tree
Model Scout; Benchmark Agent; Task Classifier; Route Optimizer; Cost Analyst; Quality Evaluator; Latency Agent; Privacy Router; Provider Health Agent; Fallback Agent; Cache Optimizer; Migration/Retirement Agent.

## Deterministic services
Price normalization; token/media accounting; budget/quota checks; privacy eligibility; region eligibility; capability matching; stable ranking; fallback ordering; circuit breakers; cache keys; telemetry aggregation; model-version pinning; spend alerts.

## Workflow
Task request → classify task/sensitivity/SLA → enumerate eligible routes → remove privacy/capability/quota/budget violations → estimate cost/quality/latency → choose deterministic best route → execute through provider abstraction → verify outcome → record telemetry/cost → fallback only by ordered policy on failure → feed benchmark/route evaluation.

## Integrations / API / data
Model providers, local/self-hosted runtimes, AI gateways, eval frameworks, observability, billing/usage, data-residency policy and agent platforms. Data: model metadata, prices, benchmarks, route decisions, health, quotas, costs, quality outcomes; no unnecessary prompt retention.

## Monetization / distribution
Requests/tokens, managed spend, percentage of verified savings, gateway fee, enterprise/private, benchmark packs and API/SDK. Distribution via AI infrastructure/dev platforms and enterprise FinOps/AI governance channels.

## Security/privacy/legal
Provider selection must honor data classification/residency and customer contracts before cost. Secrets stay in provider vaults; route evidence must explain why a model was eligible. Avoid benchmark manipulation and undisclosed quality degradation.

## Failure / edge cases
Provider price change, benchmark drift, model alias changes, outage, quota depletion, token-estimation error, cached stale answer, local model unavailable, multimodal mismatch, safety/policy differences, quality metric gaming, latency spikes, silent provider model update.

## Scale / overlap
Single gateway → enterprise AI FinOps → global model control plane. Overlap Command Center P6.2, #3 AI QC, #95 ROI. #068 commercializes routing optimization; Command Center needs an internal version now.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** provider/model abstraction, immutable version identity, route policy, cost/quality/latency/privacy telemetry, deterministic fallback, free-first preference.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already needs these in P6.2; portfolio reverse-map confirms this is foundational.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** external tenant gateway, metering and customer policy.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial benchmarks/providers/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global routing fabric and sophisticated multi-provider arbitrage.
